title: UK CPI, February 2027 (ONS, 07:00 London / 03:00 ET) — where the 2027 weights and basket are APPLIED, nine days after the article that publishes them
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukfebruary2027, fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200, 42,073 bytes) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Consumer price inflation, UK: February 2027', 'Provisional release date: 24 March 2027 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', under the UK Statistics Authority accredited-official-statistics kitemark. That is 07:00 London on a Wednesday. Re-verified independently of BOTH proposing lanes during the never-assessed initial research of this event, 2026-09-10. ONS's own label is Provisional, which is the honest reason for `estimate` on top of the standing schema gap: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:) has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics, and this lane may not self-confirm
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-10, superseding proposals/uk-cpi-2027-03-24.from-uk-cpi-2027-02-17.json and proposals/uk-cpi-2027-03-24.from-uk-cpi-2027-04-21.json (both read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). BOTH PROPOSALS' FINDINGS STAND, AND ARE NOW CARRIED BY A STRONGER SOURCE THAN EITHER USED. The uk-cpi-2027-02-17 lane identified this print as the venue for ONS's SECOND weights update and the annual basket update from the 2026 updating-weights article plus a 6-of-6 empirical match on MM23 CJXA; the uk-cpi-2027-04-21 lane identified it as the second of two CPI prints the 2027-04-29 MPC sees and as the last wholly pre-lapse reference month. This lane re-derived both from ONS's CONSUMER PRICES INDICES TECHNICAL MANUAL (fetched direct 2026-09-10, HTTP 200, 1,135,561 bytes), which states the design as standing METHODOLOGY rather than as an annual announcement: 'Weights are currently updated in two stages every year ... once with the January index to take account of the new annual COICOP weights, and once in the following month to take account of the changes to the basket of representative items', and 'At the second update of weights, PUBLISHED WITH THE FEBRUARY INDEX, the same underlying [year y-2] expenditure is updated to January of year y.' ONS's own February 2026 bulletin says it in the past tense: 'The second update has been introduced, along with the usual basket update, with the February indices.' THE ONE CORRECTION THIS LANE ADDS, AND IT MOVES THE DATE A THIRD TIME: the weight NUMBER is not first observable here. ONS publishes it in the updating-weights article and its class-level Annex A, which has landed BEFORE the February print in all ten years 2017-2026 and by 8-9 days in the last six (2021 9d, 2022 9d, 2023 9d, 2024 9d, 2025 8d, 2026 9d — Monday to Wednesday in five of the six; article dates read direct from the ONS previousreleases index, February-index publication dates read direct from the bulletin archive, both 2026-09-10). Fitted for 2027: 2027-03-15, proposed in this PR as ons-cpi-updating-weights-2027-03-15. So this print is where the 2027 weights are APPLIED; the article is where they are PUBLISHED, and a lane that wants the number scores it nine days earlier. SECOND CORRECTION, SMALLER AND EXACT: both proposals and both proposing titles say '02:00 ET'. On 2027-03-24 that is wrong by an hour. US clocks advance 2027-03-14 and UK clocks not until 2027-03-28, so this print alone of the TEN uk-cpi entries on this calendar falls inside the transatlantic DST gap: 07:00 GMT = 03:00 EDT. Every other uk-cpi entry converts to 02:00 ET; this one does not. FEBRUARY IS THE QUIETEST PLACE THE ELECTRICITY INDEX GOES: MM23 D7DT February m/m was EXACTLY +0.000% in seven of eight price-cap-era years (2019-2026), mean +0.011%, largest +0.087% — 3rd quietest of twelve months and roughly four times quieter than the March print the sibling lane already called an anchor. At the 2026 weight CJXA 20.6065/1000 the worst February move on record is 0.0018pp of headline, one FIFTY-FIFTH of the ~0.098pp electricity-VAT step. This is the last wholly pre-lapse observation of a UK CPI print (SI 2026/987's zero rate ends 2027-03-31) and it should be recorded as an anchor, never decomposed. WHAT A RESEARCHER SHOULD NOT DO WITH THIS ENTRY: read the reweighting as readable in the headline. This lane tested its own hunch and refuted it — February's median absolute y/y step is 0.300pp, second-highest of twelve against a 0.200pp all-month median, but a permutation test drawing 17 months from the all-month pool reproduces that median 26.5% of the time (D7G7 2010-2026, n=17 vs 182). Not significant; not carried. CORRIDOR: this print publishes into EASTER WEEK — Good Friday 2027-03-26 and the Easter Monday gilt closure 2027-03-29 are both on this calendar, so a UK-rates reaction window is two sessions and then a four-day weekend — five days after March quad-witching (opex-2027-03-19, high), the same morning as boj-minutes-2027-03-24, and six days after the 2027-03-18 MPC that two sibling lanes have proposed and nobody has yet made canonical. Tiered LOW on the same measurement as every UK entry here: symbols: [], no UK listing, gilt or sterling instrument on this calendar, and no rates- or FX-keyed house playbook. THE VAT CONTENT IS CONTINGENT on the 2027-03-31 lapse (FT-uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01-1); if the zero rate is extended or SI 2026/987 annulled, this print keeps its date, its weights role and its basket role, and loses only the pre-lapse-anchor framing. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action. Ledger: docs/research/events/uk-cpi-2027-03-24.md
